== Biography ==
'''Ann or Anne Glasgow''' was born about 1847 in County Antrim, Ireland. She was the daughter of [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]] and [[McCaughan-222|Mary McCaughan]].

In 1851 she was recorded as their four-year-old daughter in the family household at Lisnagaver, Rasharkin parish, County Antrim.<ref name="Census1851">[https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/pages/1851/Antrim/Kilconway/Rasharkin/Lisnagaver/35/ National Archives of Ireland, 1851 census], Alexander Glasgow household, Lisnagaver, house 35.</ref>

On 13 October 1876 Ann married '''Robert McCracken''' at Ballymoney. The register describes Robert as a full-age bachelor and farmer of Lisnagaver, son of William McCracken, labourer. Ann was a full-age spinster of Lisnagaver and named her father as Alexander Glasgow, labourer. Samuel Taylor and Mary Ann Henry witnessed the marriage.<ref name="Marriage1876">General Register Office of Ireland, civil marriage register, Robert McCracken and Ann Glasgow, 13 October 1876; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1876/11181/8097170.pdf digital image].</ref>

Their known child, [[McCracken-5690|William James McCracken]], was born at Lisnagaver on 21 September 1877. His birth registration names Robert McCracken, labourer, and Ann formerly Glasgow as his parents.<ref name="WilliamBirth1877">General Register Office of Ireland, civil birth register, William James McCracken, 21 September 1877, Lisnagaver; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1877/03001/2099809.pdf digital image].</ref> William died there the following day, aged one day, from debility from birth; Ann registered both events.<ref name="WilliamDeath1877">General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register, William James McCracken, 22 September 1877, Lisnagaver; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1877/020541/7208135.pdf digital image].</ref>

Ann died in 1898 in the Calton registration district of Glasgow, Lanarkshire, Scotland, aged 49, recorded as '''Ann McCracken''' with maiden surname Glasgow and mother's maiden surname McCaughern.<ref name="AnnDeath1898">National Records of Scotland, statutory registers of deaths, 1898, Calton (Glasgow), 644/4 70: Ann McCracken, female, 49, other surname Glasgow, mother's maiden surname McCaughern. [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ ScotlandsPeople] index, searched 23 September 2026; register image not yet viewed.</ref> The maiden name, her mother's maiden name and her age, consistent with the four-year-old Ann of 1851, identify her with Alexander and Mary's daughter. Calton was also where her brother [[Glasgow-938|Robert Glasgow]] had settled. The register entry, not yet viewed, should give her exact date and place of death, her husband's name and status, and an informant. No later record of Robert McCracken has yet been securely identified.

== Research Notes ==
No compatible WikiTree profile has yet been identified for Ann's husband Robert McCracken. A same-name Ballymena mechanic who died in 1880 was the husband of Rose Ann Black and son of John McCracken, and was a different man.

This profile was originally created in 2015 to be Anna, born 1847 in Plains, Lanarkshire, Scotland. She was the daughter of [[Glasgow-424|John Glasgow]] and [[Forsyth-878|Christina Forsyth]].

This profile was vandalized in 2016 removing relationships and then this profile was merged with a different profile with different parents, so a new profile [[Glasgow-2083|Anna Glasgow (1847-)]] has been created since this profile has now been merged and changed to different parents.  History for that original profile information is in this profile.


The informant who registered [[Glasgow-951|Alexander Glasgow]]'s death at Gortahar in 1888 was formerly read here as '''Nancy Glasgow''' and compared with Ann. Read against the same registrar's other entries, the forename is '''Mary''': it matches his "Mary" in three nearby entries and differs from his "Nancy" in a fourth. The informant, "Mary Glasgow, daughter", is therefore not Ann. She was most probably Ann's sister [[Glasgow-3167|Mary]], by then Mrs Elder of Gortahar, entered under her maiden surname. The online image is the registrar's quarterly copy; the local register has not been viewed.<ref name="AlexanderDeath1888">General Register Office of Ireland, civil death register, death of Alexander Glasgow, 16 May 1888, Gortahar; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/deaths_returns/deaths_1888/06179/4766466.pdf digital image].</ref>

A possible identification concerns Ann Glasgow. The original civil birth return records Mary Ellen, a female child born at Lisnagaver on 14 February 1867. The mother is Mary Glasgow; no father is entered.<ref>Ballymoney/Ahoghill civil birth register 1867; [https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/birth_returns/births_1867/03501/2286677.pdf record].</ref> The identification remains uncertain.
